title: From complexity to clarity.
visual: Scattered information tiles converge into one clean Explain mark.
lines: An answer can be correct, and still be hard to understand.
Explain turns complex ideas into something you can see, follow, and remember.

title: Start with the learning goal.
visual: A natural-language request resolves into topic, audience, and outcome.
lines: Start with a topic, a document, or a piece of code.
The skill identifies your audience and what they should understand afterward.
You can specify the format, length, and budget.

title: The idea chooses the medium.
visual: Four animated format cards reveal prose, diagram, interactive page, and video.
lines: A definition may need a sentence. A relationship may need a diagram.
Changing a variable calls for an interactive page.
A process unfolding over time may work best as a narrated video.

title: Show what a cache changes.
visual: First request travels to the origin. A repeat request takes the shorter cache route.
lines: Take a cache. The first request fetches data from its original source.
A later request can reuse the stored copy.
Animating those two paths makes the difference visible.

title: Every scene earns its place.
visual: Evidence becomes a plain-language script, then an ordered storyboard.
lines: Explain checks the source material, defines unfamiliar terms, and writes in plain language.
Then it maps each teaching point to a scene.
The visuals show the mechanism while narration connects the ideas.

title: Purposeful motion. Clear ideas.
visual: Remotion video card, GSAP interaction card, and Motion Canvas vector card animate distinct examples.
lines: Remotion is the default for polished video.
G sap supports interactive web animation. Motion Canvas suits narrated vector diagrams.
Typography, color, and motion stay consistent so your attention follows the idea.

title: Narration sets the pace.
visual: Local Kokoro voice waveform generates separate reusable audio clips.
lines: For this film, Kokoro generates the narration locally, with no paid speech API.
Each passage becomes a reusable audio clip.
Changing the visuals does not require generating the voice again.

title: One timeline. Everything aligned.
visual: Audio, animation, and caption tracks align to a shared moving playhead.
lines: The skill measures the actual audio, then fits the animation to it.
Captions follow the spoken passages.
Frame based motion keeps previews and final renders consistent.

title: A render is only the beginning.
visual: Rendered frame enlarges while checks inspect labels, timing, audio, and export.
lines: Before delivery, it checks rendered frames, readable labels, timing, captions, and the exported file.
Audio should be checked for pronunciation and clipping.
Any checks it could not perform are reported clearly.

title: Make the next idea click.
visual: Explain command appears above three harness chips and a finished-artifact stack.
lines: Use Explain in Codex, OpenCode, or Claude Code.
Ask for the explanation you need, and receive the finished artifact plus editable source.
This video was created using that same workflow.
